verification.notes: Draft: no Cambridge International examiner or school reviewer has checked this pack. Source links: all six URLs resolved to the named pages on 2026-10-21 (titles matched). The IGCSE subject list on the Cambridge IGCSE page confirms that the board runs both A*-G syllabuses (for example Accounting 0452) and 9-1 syllabuses (Accounting (9-1) 0985), which is why this pack ships both scales. What is a placeholder, not a claim: every percentage-to-grade band. Cambridge sets grade thresholds for each syllabus option and each exam series after marking, so igcse_a_star_g, igcse_9_1 and cambridge_a_level are school defaults and are declared overridable (grading_scales.<code>.bands); a school must replace them with the board's thresholds for the session. What is structured but unverified: the 0580 extended-tier paper maxima (Paper 2 = 70 marks, Paper 4 = 130 marks, weights 0.35/0.65) follow the published syllabus and were not re-read from the syllabus PDF; AS and A Level subjects declare no papers, and the A Level Mathematics paper set is not modelled, because only the IGCSE papers and no A Level maxima were verified. The IGCSE papers carry their 0.35/0.65 weights in component_policy.weights under MAT, and Mathematics declares igcse_a_star_g at Y10-Y11 because the modelled 0580 papers are the A*-G syllabus. UCAS: the A Level tariff is per grade, not per grade and subject: A* 56, A 48, B 40, C 32, D 24, E 16, U 0, summed over the qualifications the candidate takes. The tariff table is rendered client-side and was not read off the live page, so the figures come from spec 03 Appendix C; no AS or IGCSE tariff is modelled. Grade codes are the printed grades, so A* is the band code and the label repeats it. Calendar: the pack declares both the northern (August) and the southern (January) academic year as named variants, northern by default, as spec 03 Appendix C asks. Locale: English only; other languages are a translation task, not a pack version.
